A tension arises between depth (continued compression in the current domain) and breadth (sampling new domains). Formally, this is an exploration-exploitation tradeoff at the meta-level of curriculum selection: the agent must balance the diminishing returns of further practice against the uncertain but potentially high returns of novel domains. This can be addressed via upper confidence bound (UCB)-style heuristics. Let ΔL̂(π)\widehat{\Delta L}(\pi) be the mean estimated compression gain and σ(π)\sigma(\pi) its uncertainty (e.g., posterior standard deviation). A UCB-style policy scores each option as: The concepts are summarized schematically (Figure).

U(π)=ΔL̂(π)+ασ(π),U(\pi) = \widehat{\Delta L}(\pi) + \alpha \, \sigma(\pi), where α>0\alpha > 0 controls the exploration bonus. Large α\alpha favors breadth (exploring uncertain domains); small α\alpha favors depth (exploiting known high-yield domains).

Another complicating factor is the need to account for analogical mapping: deep compression in one domain can yield representations that transfer to others, meaning the true value of depth is not just local ΔL\Delta L but the expected compression gain across all domains sharing latent structure. An agent that masters music theory may find physics more compressible; one that learns chess may compress strategic reasoning generally. This transforms the depth-breadth tradeoff from a simple bandit problem into a structured one where the reward function itself depends on the similarity kernel over domains–favoring depth in "hub" domains with high transfer potential over isolated curiosities. The concepts are summarized schematically (Figure).

This leads us to failure modes; the compression-progress drive is not always adaptive. Pathological cases include:

Novelty addiction: Over-weighting exploration (α→∞\alpha \to \infty in the UCB formulation above) prevents sustained engagement; the agent "surfs" novelty without deep compression.

Compulsive systematizing: Over-investment in domains with high local ΔL\Delta L but low transfer value, i.e., ΔLlocal≫0\Delta L_{\text{local}} \gg 0 but 𝔼[ΔLtransfer]≈0\mathbb{E}[\Delta L_{\text{transfer}}] \approx 0.

Boredom intolerance: Some skill acquisition requires tolerance of the low-ΔL\Delta L consolidation phase; agents with steep temporal discounting on rintr^{\mathrm{int}} may abandon skills prematurely.

These failure modes suggest that the raw compression-progress signal must be modulated by higher-order objectives–pragmatic value, social relevance, long-term goal structure–to produce adaptive behavior
